title: Adopt CAS-backed remote build cache, consolidate builder images, and modernize toolchains
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Our monorepo builds have regressed in median CI time and cache hit variability across GitHub Actions matrices. Current strategies use job-level docker layer caches and a mix of hosted caches (actions/cache), which lead to inconsistent hits when job matrices change or when builder images are updated. We also have multiple ad-hoc builder images (node-builder, go-builder, python-builder) that diverge and pull toolchain installers at runtime, increasing variability and image sizes.

Scope: This ticket consolidates three technical areas into a single, measurable initiative: 1) migrate CI build caching to a Content Addressable Storage (CAS)-backed remote cache (eg. buildkit + registry or cloud CAS), 2) standardize and reduce builder image surface by creating a small set of hermetic builder images (multi-arch, slim) and a reproducible layer layout, and 3) upgrade and pin primary toolchains (Go 1.21 -> 1.22, Node 18 -> 20) and linters with clear migration paths. The goal is to reduce median CI build time by >=25% for common PRs and to increase cache hit rates on PRs by >=40%.

Out of scope: full migration of all legacy repos that follow different release cadences (will be tracked as follow-ups), moving to self-hosted runners (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: CAS remote cache integrated with BuildKit and reachable from GitHub Actions (proof via build logs)
Median CI build time for the default PR workflow reduced by >=25% compared to baseline (baseline recorded 2025-01-30)
Cache hit rate for typical PR builds increased by >=40% (measured over a 7-day window after rollout)
Hermetic builder images created (node/go/python) with image sizes reduced by >=30% vs current builders and documented Dockerfile layout
Toolchains pinned and upgraded: Go 1.22 and Node 20 available in builders, migration notes and at least one downstream service successfully built/tested
No regressions in linting: ESLint and golangci-lint versions updated with rule compatibility notes and any breaking rules documented
Rollout plan executed with canary on open-source and non-critical services before org-wide rollout

Add buildkit cache exporter/importer to workflows

notes: Tradeoffs: Moving to CAS requires more storage and different retention policies; we'll prototype with compressed blobs and garbage collection windows to control costs.
Risk: Some third-party actions do not support registry cache exporter; fallback is to use actions/cache for those jobs until we can replace them.
If cache keys are too granular we lose cross-job benefits; aim for content-addressed keys derived from Dockerfile/content and toolchain manifest.
